title: Module-to-Hub link must be RJ-45 8P8C (not Mini-Fit Jr)
rule: Every module-to-Hub interface connector must be RJ-45 8P8C. No Mini-Fit Jr (5569/5557/87427/45586) footprint may appear on link nets (CAN_H, CAN_L, DETECT, STREAM_P, STREAM_N, VCC/+5VSB). Exception: J3/J4 on the 24-pin ATX module are Mini-Fit Jr on the PSU-side power path — that is §2.8 compliant.
scope: All boards: any net containing CAN, DETECT, STREAM, 5VSB, or VCC — check every component on those nets for Mini-Fit footprint keywords (5569, 5557, 87427, 45586, mini-fit)
rationale: Mini-Fit Jr was retired as the module-to-Hub interconnect platform-wide. RJ-45 is the universal locked interface for all tiers.
source: CLAUDE.md 'Locked decisions' section — 'Module-to-Hub connector is RJ-45 (8P8C) for all tiers. Mini-Fit Jr is retired as the module-to-Hub interconnect'
check_method: For every footprint on CAN/DETECT/STREAM/VCC nets: check footprint string for mini-fit/5569/5557/87427/45586 keywords. Flag any match.

title: RJ-45 pins 4+5 = STREAM_P/STREAM_N on Pro+ only; Standard leaves unused
rule: On Standard-tier boards: RJ-45 pins 4 and 5 must NOT be connected to an RS-485 transceiver. On Pro+ boards: pins 4 and 5 carry STREAM_P (RS-485) and STREAM_N respectively.
scope: Derivable from board profile (cfg.profile). Standard boards: J1 pins 4 and 5 are NC or terminated at module side. Pro+ boards: nets must contain STREAM.
rationale: RS-485 streaming is Pro+ only per §3.2. A Standard module with STREAM active wastes power and violates tiering.
source: CLAUDE.md pin allocation table — 'Pin 4: STREAM_P (Pro+); Pin 5: STREAM_N (Pro+)'; locked decisions 'Standard does not populate it'
check_method: For Standard profile: net_of(rj45, '4') and net_of(rj45, '5') must not contain 'STREAM'; chk_rs485_tiering verifies no RS-485 IC present.

title: RJ-45 pin 7 = reserved spare, NOT AUX_REF
rule: RJ-45 pin 7 must be a reserved spare. If connected, the net name must NOT contain 'AUX' or 'REF'. Pin 7 was formerly considered for a distributed voltage reference; that use was rejected in v1.1 (OQ-3 resolved).
scope: All boards with an RJ-45 connector: net_of(J1, '7') must not match AUX|REF pattern
rationale: OQ-3 resolved: no distributed reference; pin 7 is a reserved spare. Assigning it AUX_REF would mislead firmware on any tier.
source: CLAUDE.md pin allocation table — 'Pin 7: Reserved spare (no distributed reference; OQ-3 resolved)'
check_method: net_of(rj45_ref, '7'): if not None/NC, assert not re.search(r'AUX|REF', net, re.I)

title: DETECT code resistor = 2.2kΩ on CAN-only Standard modules
rule: For CAN-only Standard modules (24-pin ATX, EPS 8-pin, PCIe 8-pin, 12VHPWR Standard): the resistor on the DETECT net to GND must be 2.2kΩ ±10%. This encodes CAN-only link capability per the §2.3 code table.
scope: Boards: atx-24pin, eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port, 12vhpwr-standard. DETECT net resistors (R* where one end is on DETECT net and other is GND).
rationale: §2.3 DETECT code table is LOCKED. CAN-only = 2.2kΩ. An incorrect value makes the Hub misidentify the module capability.
source: CLAUDE.md DETECT section — 'CAN-only 2.2kΩ (0.595V)'; chk_detect_resistor default want=2200.0
check_method: Find resistors on DETECT net with other terminal on GND. Parse resistance value. Assert abs(value - 2200) / 2200 < 0.1.

title: DETECT code resistor = 4.7kΩ on CAN+RS-485 Pro modules
rule: For modules with CAN+RS-485 (12VHPWR Pro): the DETECT resistor to GND must be 4.7kΩ ±10%.
scope: Boards: 12vhpwr-pro. DETECT net resistors.
rationale: §2.3 DETECT code table is LOCKED. CAN+RS-485 = 4.7kΩ (1.055V on the Hub's 10kΩ/3.3V divider).
source: CLAUDE.md DETECT section — 'CAN+RS-485 4.7kΩ (1.055V)'; '12VHPWR Pro is CAN+RS-485 (4.7kΩ)'
check_method: For profile=pro boards with RS-485 IC: DETECT resistor must be ~4700Ω. chk_detect_resistor needs cfg.params['detect_ohms'] = 4700.
existing_checker: chk_detect_resistor in cec_synth_pipeline.py CONFORMANCE stage (needs per-board detect_ohms param override)

title: DETECT 10kΩ pull-up to 3.3V is on the Hub, NOT on modules
rule: The 10kΩ pull-up resistor on the DETECT line must appear only on Hub boards (connected between DETECT net and +3V3 or 3V3_ADC). Module boards must NOT have a pull-up on their DETECT net (they only have the code resistor to GND).
scope: Hub boards: verify 10kΩ between DETECT and 3.3V. Module boards: verify no pull-up (no resistor with one terminal on DETECT and other on 3V3/VCC).
rationale: A module-side pull-up would create a resistor divider with the Hub's 10kΩ pull-up, corrupting the DETECT voltage reading and the module ID. The Hub's 3.3V reference (not 5VSB VCC) keeps the ADC in range.
source: CLAUDE.md DETECT section — 'a fixed 10kΩ pull-up to its 3.3V ADC reference (NOT the 5VSB VCC pin)'
check_method: On Hub board: find R* where net_of(R, pin_a) contains DETECT AND net_of(R, pin_b) contains '3V3'; assert value ~10kΩ. On module boards: assert no such pull-up present.

title: DETECT pin-8 ESD clamp diode (PESD5V0S1BA SOD-323) on every board
rule: Every Hub port and every module must carry a low-capacitance ESD diode on the DETECT line: cathode to DETECT net, anode to GND. Part must be PESD5V0S1BA (SOD-323, LCSC C5261083). The PESD5V0S1UL (DFN1006/SOD-882) is NOT interchangeable — it cannot be assembled in the SOD-323 land.
scope: All boards. Hub Standard: D2-D5 (one per port). Modules: D1. BOM field: Value='PESD5V0S1BA', LCSC='C5261083'.
rationale: Locked §2.4 v2.0: hot-plug insertion on the bare DETECT analog input (directly into an ESP32 ADC) risks ESD damage. The low-cap diode clamps the pin without loading the ADC divider.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'one low-capacitance ESD diode on the DETECT pin (pin 8 -> ESP32 ADC) on EVERY Hub and module'; 'PESD5V0S1BA in SOD-323 (LCSC C5261083)'
check_method: Find diode(s) on DETECT net. Check footprint is SOD-323. Check BOM Value=PESD5V0S1BA and LCSC=C5261083. Check cathode=DETECT, anode=GND.

title: PESD5V0S1UL must not appear on any SOD-323 DETECT ESD land
rule: The value PESD5V0S1UL must NOT appear on any DETECT ESD clamp whose footprint is SOD-323. The UL suffix is a DFN1006 / SOD-882 package that cannot be assembled in the SOD-323 courtyard.
scope: All boards: any component named PESD5V0S1UL on a footprint containing 'SOD-323' or 'SOD323'
rationale: Generator emits PESD5V0S1UL by default but the physically ordered part (the SOD-323 sibling) is PESD5V0S1BA. Mixing them causes assembly failure.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'part corrected from PESD5V0S1UL to the SOD-323 sibling PESD5V0S1BA... the UL is only stocked in DFN1006/SOD-882 by LCSC, the BA is the SOD-323 part'
check_method: For every component where Value='PESD5V0S1UL': check footprint string for 'SOD-323'. Flag any match.

title: CAN transceiver must be TJA1051T/3 (never TJA1462A)
rule: Every board carrying a CAN transceiver must use TJA1051T/3 (classical CAN, SO-8, LCSC C38695). The TJA1462A (CAN-FD/SIC part) is explicitly banned platform-wide. No other CAN transceiver part number is permitted without a spec revision.
scope: All boards with CAN (all tiers). U2 on modules, U2 on Hub Standard. BOM field Value='TJA1051T/3', LCSC='C38695'.
rationale: CAN-FD is deferred platform-wide (spec §3.1 v3.5). TJA1051T/3 is cheaper (~$0.40), better stocked, and pin-compatible. TJA1462A on the bus forces FD-rate negotiation and may assert SIC modes.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'LOCKED to the classical part (spec §3.1 v3.5)... TJA1051T/3... The unused cec-vendor:TJA1462AT symbol is left in the lib (harmless; not referenced by any board)'
check_method: For every footprint matching SO-8 or SOIC-8 on CAN_H/CAN_L nets: assert Value='TJA1051T/3' and LCSC='C38695'. Flag any Value containing 'TJA1462' or 'FD'.

title: No CAN-FD transceiver (TJA1462A or similar) on any board
rule: Component values must not contain 'TJA1462' or other CAN-FD transceiver part numbers. CAN-FD is deferred platform-wide.
scope: All boards: BOM Value fields must not match TJA1462, CAN-FD, TCAN455, TCAN4550
rationale: CAN-FD deferred platform-wide. A single non-FD module forces the whole bus to classical; an FD part wastes cost and can cause protocol confusion.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'CAN-FD DEFERRED platform-wide... TJA1051T/3 is cheaper... no longer earns its place'
check_method: For all components: assert Value does not match regex r'TJA1462|CAN.FD|TCAN45'

title: CAN termination: fixed 120Ω split termination at Hub only; no module termination
rule: The CAN bus termination must be a fixed split 120Ω at the Hub (two 60Ω resistors in series across CAN_H/CAN_L with a 4.7nF cap from the midpoint to GND). Module boards must carry NO resistor bridging CAN_H and CAN_L in the 100-140Ω range.
scope: Hub boards: verify two ~60Ω resistors between CAN_H and CAN_L with a cap midpoint. Module boards: no 100-140Ω across CAN_H/CAN_L.
rationale: Classical CAN bus integrity requires exactly one termination point at the Hub for star topology. Module-side termination creates multiple terminations corrupting signal integrity.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'Termination: fixed 120 ohm split at Hub'; chk_no_module_can_term enforces module side
check_method: On Hub: find R pair bridging CAN_H and CAN_L with midpoint cap. On modules: chk_no_module_can_term (100-140Ω check).
existing_checker: chk_no_module_can_term in cec_synth_pipeline.py CONFORMANCE stage (module side)

title: 24-pin ATX module: 4× INA228 (one per rail: 12V, 5V, 3V3, 5VSB)
rule: The 24-pin ATX module must carry exactly 4 INA228 (20-bit, VSSOP-10) instances. INA238 is explicitly NOT acceptable (it is a pin-compatible drop-in but different part). Each INA228 must be on a distinct rail shunt (12V, 5V, 3V3, 5VSB).
scope: Board: atx-24pin. Count components where Value='INA228' or Value contains 'INA228'. Assert count=4.
rationale: §6.1 specifies INA228 for the 24-pin module — 20-bit resolution with hardware energy/charge accumulators, required for energy reporting per OQ-13. INA238 lacks the energy accumulator.
source: CLAUDE.md module sensing — '24-pin ATX: 4x INA228 (20-bit, 195uV bus LSB, internal energy/charge accumulators), one per rail'
check_method: Filter nl.comps by board=atx-24pin and Value containing 'INA228'. Assert count==4. Assert no INA238 present.

title: EPS 8-pin module: INA238 per cable (1-2 cables)
rule: The EPS 8-pin module must carry INA238 current-sense ICs (VSSOP-10, I2C), one per cable, with 1-2 cables populated.
scope: Board: eps-8pin. Count components where Value contains 'INA238'. Assert count in [1,2].
rationale: §6.1 specifies INA238 per cable for EPS. Per-cable granularity is the design intent (not per-pin).
source: CLAUDE.md module sensing — 'EPS 8-pin: INA238 per cable (per-cable granularity), 2 cables populated'
check_method: Filter nl.comps for board=eps-8pin, Value='INA238*'. Assert 1<=count<=2.

title: PCIe 8-pin modules: INA238 per cable (2-3 cables per SKU)
rule: PCIe 8-pin 2-port must have 2 INA238. PCIe 8-pin 3-port must have 3 INA238. Maximum is 3 cables per spec §6.2.
scope: Board: pcie-8pin-2port -> assert INA238 count=2; pcie-8pin-3port -> assert INA238 count=3.
rationale: §6.2 PCIe sensing is per-cable INA238. The board SKU name encodes the cable count.
source: CLAUDE.md module sensing — 'PCIe 8-pin: INA238 per cable, 3 cables populated (spec upper bound)'
check_method: Board name -> expected count map {pcie-8pin-2port:2, pcie-8pin-3port:3}. Count INA238 in nl.comps.

title: 12VHPWR Standard module: exactly 6× INA240A3 (D package, SOIC-8)
rule: The 12VHPWR Standard module must carry exactly 6 INA240 current-sense amplifiers, one per pin of the 12V-2x6 connector. Part must be INA240A3 D-package (SOIC-8 / INA240A3DR), NEVER the PW (TSSOP) package which has a different pinout.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. Count components where Value='INA240A3' or 'INA240'. Assert count=6. Assert LCSC=C2060584 (the D/SOIC-8 part).
rationale: §6.1 specifies 6× INA240 per-pin. SOIC-8 (D) and TSSOP (PW) INA240A3 have different pinouts — a PW assembled on a D land creates a functional failure.
source: CLAUDE.md module sensing — '12VHPWR Standard: six INA240 per-pin current-sense amps into the ESP32-S3 ADC'; 'the orderable MPN MUST be the D part (INA240A3DR), never the PW'
check_method: Board=12vhpwr-standard: count INA240* in nl.comps, assert=6. Check BOM LCSC for C2060584. Flag any 'PW' or TSSOP footprint.

title: 12VHPWR Standard INA240: REF1 and REF2 tied to GND (unidirectional forward sensing)
rule: On the 12VHPWR Standard module, all INA240 instances must have REF1 (pin 7) and REF2 (pin 3) connected to GND — not to a precision reference. This sets unidirectional forward-only sensing.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. For each INA240 (U*): net_of(U, '3') must be GND, net_of(U, '7') must be GND.
rationale: The 12VHPWR Standard module uses the INA240 analog output directly into the ESP32 ADC without a signed reference — tying REF1/REF2 to GND gives unidirectional (positive current only) measurement with output centered at GND+offset.
source: CLAUDE.md module sensing — 'REF1/REF2 tied to GND (unidirectional forward sensing)'
check_method: For each INA240 instance: assert net_of(ref, '3') in GND nets AND net_of(ref, '7') in GND nets.

title: 12VHPWR Pro module: INA240 + LTC2358-18 + REF3033 (not REF3030)
rule: The 12VHPWR Pro module must carry: (a) INA240A3 per-pin current-sense amps, (b) an LTC2358-18 8-channel simultaneous-sampling 18-bit SAR ADC, (c) REF3033 (3.3V precision reference feeding the LTC2358 reference input). REF3030 (3.0V) must NOT be used — it is the Standard module's ADC-measured reference.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-pro. BOM must include LTC2358, REF3033. Must NOT include REF3030.
rationale: §6.1 specifies LTC2358-18 for the Pro module's simultaneous-sampling architecture. REF3033 feeds the LTC2358 reference at 3.3V; REF3030 (3.0V) is only for the Standard module's ADC-measurement ratiometric correction.
source: CLAUDE.md module sensing — '12VHPWR Pro module: ESP32-P4, INA240A3 per-pin current-sense amps on per-pin shunts, LTC2358-18 8-channel simultaneous-sampling 18-bit SAR ADC'; v3.8 note 'Standard REF3030=3.0V is MEASURED by the ADC; the Pro's REF3033=3.3V feeds the LTC2358 ref'
check_method: Board=12vhpwr-pro: assert INA240* count>=6, assert any Value='LTC2358*', assert any Value='REF3033'. Assert no Value='REF3030'.

title: 12VHPWR Standard module: REF3030 (3.0V) ADC-measured ratiometric reference
rule: The 12VHPWR Standard module must include U4 = REF3030 (3.0V, SOT-23, LCSC C38423) with its output connected to an ESP32 ADC pin (IO8/ADC1). This enables ratiometric correction of the rail divider and INA240 output readings.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. BOM must include REF3030. Footprint: DBZ3/SOT-23. LCSC=C38423.
rationale: v3.8 spec: REF3030 lifts rail-divider + all 6 INA240 currents from ~±1% to ~±0.3-0.5% (OQ-8 RESOLVED). Without it accuracy is limited to the ESP32 ADC reference drift.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.8 section — 'U4 = REF3030 (3.0V, SOT-23, cec-vendor:REF3030, MPN REF3030AIDBZR)... LCSC C38423'
check_method: Board=12vhpwr-standard: assert any Value='REF3030', LCSC='C38423'. Assert REF3030 output net connects to an ESP32 ADC pin net.

title: 24-pin ATX module 5VSB shunt: 25mΩ
rule: The 24-pin ATX module shunt on the 5VSB rail must be 25mΩ (0.025Ω). The 5VSB rail carries much lower current than the main rails, requiring a higher-value shunt for measurement resolution.
scope: Board: atx-24pin. The shunt resistor on the 5VSB sense net must be ~0.025Ω.
rationale: §6.4 LOCKED: '24-pin 5VSB = 25mΩ'. 5VSB current is milliamps in standby — a 2mΩ shunt would produce unmeasurably small voltage drops.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'Shunt values: 24-pin 5VSB = 25mΩ'
check_method: Board=atx-24pin: find shunt on 5VSB net (net name contains '5VSB'). Assert _r_value_ohms(value) ~= 0.025 (within 20%).
existing_checker: chk_shunt_values in cec_synth_pipeline.py CONFORMANCE stage (needs 5VSB-specific override)

title: EPS and PCIe modules: 0.5mΩ per-cable shunt
rule: EPS 8-pin and PCIe 8-pin module shunts must each be 0.5mΩ (0.0005Ω). One shunt per cable.
scope: Boards: eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port. All RS* shunts. Assert value ~0.0005Ω.
rationale: §6.4 LOCKED: 'EPS and PCIe per-cable = 0.5mΩ'. EPS/PCIe cables carry 40-55A peak; 0.5mΩ limits power dissipation while giving measurable voltage drop for the INA238.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'Shunt values: EPS/PCIe per-cable = 0.5mΩ'
check_method: For boards in {eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port}: all RS* shunts must be ~0.0005Ω (within 20%).
existing_checker: chk_shunt_values in cec_synth_pipeline.py CONFORMANCE stage (default want=0.5e-3 — correct for EPS/PCIe)

title: 12VHPWR Standard module: 1mΩ per-pin shunts
rule: The 12VHPWR Standard module must have 6 shunts of 1mΩ (0.001Ω) each, one per +12V pin of the connector.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. RS1-RS6 shunts. Assert all ~0.001Ω.
rationale: §6.4 LOCKED: '12VHPWR per-pin = 1mΩ'. The 12V-2x6 connector carries up to 9.2A per pin; 1mΩ balances dissipation with resolution for the INA240.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'Shunt values: 12VHPWR per-pin = 1mΩ'
check_method: Board=12vhpwr-standard: all RS* must be ~0.001Ω (within 20%). Assert count=6.
existing_checker: chk_shunt_values in cec_synth_pipeline.py CONFORMANCE stage (needs per-board shunt_ohms=0.001 override)

title: Kelvin four-wire sense: _HI/_LO net pairs must straddle a 2-pad shunt
rule: Every *_HI / *_LO net pair must straddle a 2-pad shunt resistor (the _HI net connects to the force/high terminal, _LO to the sense/low terminal of the same shunt). The sense must also reach an INA input pin.
scope: All boards with _HI/_LO net pairs (EPS, PCIe, 12VHPWR Standard). Derivable from net names using _RE_KELVIN_HI pattern in cec_score.py.
rationale: §6.8 requires four-wire Kelvin sensing for accurate low-value shunt measurements. A single-point tap creates lead resistance error that dominates at 0.5-2mΩ.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'four-wire Kelvin sense (§6.8) — Kelvin geometry is a layout (GUI) task'
check_method: For each (stem_HI, stem_LO) pair from _derive_pairs(): find a 2-pad component where one pad is on _HI net and other pad is on _LO net (the shunt). Also check any INA* has a pin on _HI or _LO net.
existing_checker: chk_kelvin_topology in cec_synth_pipeline.py MEASURE stage; kelvin_ok gate in cec_score.py ROUTE_GATE

title: FTP shielded RJ-45: Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C (LCSC C2683360) with SH1/SH2 → GND
rule: All RJ-45 jacks on Hub Standard, 12VHPWR Standard, and EPS must use the Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C shielded FTP jack (LCSC C2683360, footprint cec:RJ45_FTP_Shielded_Horizontal). Shield tabs SH1 and SH2 must both be connected to GND. The C86580 (CONNFLY DS1129-05-S80BP-X dual-port jack) is explicitly WRONG — it is a 16-contact dual-port part.
scope: Boards: hub-standard (J2-J5), 12vhpwr-standard (J1), eps-8pin (J1). BOM LCSC must be C2683360. Footprint must contain 'FTP' or 'Shielded'. SH1/SH2 nets must be GND.
rationale: §2.1 LOCKS FTP shielded jacks platform-wide. Both-end shielding and grounding provides HF noise rejection on the RJ-45 link.
source: CLAUDE.md FTP shielding section — 'MPN LOCKED (single shielded 8P8C, metal shell, right-angle TH, 1.5A)... LCSC C2683360... SH1/SH2 -> GND (both-end shielding+grounding)'
check_method: For Hub/12VHPWR-Std/EPS: find J* with RJ45 footprint. Assert LCSC=C2683360 or footprint contains 'FTP'/'Shielded'. Assert net_of(J, 'SH1') in GND nets and net_of(J, 'SH2') in GND nets. Flag C86580.

title: RJ-45 connector must have documented ≥1.5A current rating
rule: The selected RJ-45 8P8C connector must have a manufacturer-documented current rating of at least 1.5A per contact. The platform-locked Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58-8P8C meets this.
scope: All RJ-45 connectors on all boards. Verifiable via BOM MPN cross-reference.
rationale: Platform VCC pin carries per-port 5VSB distribution; worst-case LED + sensing load approaches the contact rating. Below 1.5A creates thermal stress at the contact.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'Connector must have a documented current rating of at least 1.5A'
check_method: BOM check: for each RJ-45 MPN, cross-reference datasheet current rating ≥1.5A. Kinghelm C2683360 passes.

title: Hub bulk power input: dedicated 2-pin JST-XH connector (≥3A), not RJ-45 VCC
rule: Every Hub board must have a dedicated 2-pin +5VSB power-in connector (J1 on Hub Standard: JST-XH, ≥3A rated) separate from all RJ-45 ports. This connector receives bulk 5VSB from the 24-pin ATX module. The RJ-45 VCC pins carry only per-port distribution, not the trunk.
scope: Hub boards only. Verify a non-RJ-45 2-pin connector on a net containing '5VSB' or 'PWR_IN'. Assert its footprint/part is JST-XH or equivalent ≥3A.
rationale: OQ-1 RESOLVED: separate bulk power connector removes single-pin trunk constraint on the RJ-45 VCC contact (1.5A limit). All bulk flows over the JST leg.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'Hub bulk power comes in on a dedicated 2-pin +5VSB power-in connector, separate from the RJ-45 interface... Use the simplest 2-pin part rated for the full Hub trunk with margin (working selection: 2-pin JST-XH, >=3A)'
check_method: Hub boards: find connector (non-RJ-45) with 2 pins on 5VSB or power-in net. Assert footprint contains 'XH' or part is rated ≥3A. Flag if absent.

title: Hub Standard power mux: TPS2121 priority mux (not LTC4417 or discrete diodes)
rule: Hub Standard must use TPS2121 for its PSU/USB power priority mux front-end (U5, and U7 for the §2.9 3-input OR). LTC4417 is the textbook triple-prioritizer but is cost-excluded ($7.77 vs TPS2121 ~$1).
scope: Board: hub-standard. BOM must include ≥1 TPS2121RUXR (LCSC C485916). Assert no LTC4417.
rationale: §2.7 front-end reconciled as-built: TPS2121 does inrush limiting + source-side reverse-current blocking via its soft-start. The §2.9 second TPS2121 (U7) adds the MAIN_5V OR for the 3-input power cascade.
source: CLAUDE.md Hub Standard section — 'TPS2121 PSU/USB priority mux does inrush limiting via its soft-start'; action item 0 — 'cascade adds U7 = 2nd TPS2121 (C485916)'
check_method: Board=hub-standard: assert any Value='TPS2121*'. Flag any LTC4417.

title: Hub Standard MCU: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (not MINI-1)
rule: Hub Standard must use ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (16MB flash + 8MB PSRAM). No MINI-1 variant is acceptable — the MINI-1 has no 16MB SKU.
scope: Board: hub-standard. BOM Value for U1 must contain 'WROOM-1-N16R8' or 'WROOM-1' with N16R8 variant. Assert no 'MINI-1'.
rationale: Hub aggregates 4-8 ports and runs the full stack including NanoKVM data path — requires 16MB flash and 8MB PSRAM. MINI-1 tops out at 8MB flash with no PSRAM option at that size.
source: CLAUDE.md boards table — 'Hub Standard: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (16 MB flash + 8 MB PSRAM)'
check_method: Board=hub-standard, U1 (ESP32 ref): assert Value contains 'WROOM-1-N16R8'. Flag any 'MINI-1' on this board.

title: 12VHPWR Standard module MCU: ESP32-S3-MINI-1 (N4R2)
rule: The 12VHPWR Standard module must use ESP32-S3-MINI-1-N4R2 (LCSC C3013941). This is the analog-ADC module with 9 ADC inputs needed for the 6× INA240 + rail divider + REF3030 + sideband taps.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. BOM U1 Value must contain 'S3-MINI-1' or 'S3-MINI'. LCSC=C3013941.
rationale: 12VHPWR Standard uses the ESP32-S3 ADC heavily (6 INA240 outputs + 1 rail divider + REF3030 + 2 NTC + 4 sideband = 14 signals). ESP32-C6 has fewer ADC inputs.
source: CLAUDE.md module sensing — '12VHPWR Standard: ESP32-S3-MINI-1'; v3.10 note 'Hub KEEPS the S3-WROOM-1-N16R8; 12VHPWR Standard KEEPS the S3-MINI-1'
check_method: Board=12vhpwr-standard: U1 Value must contain 'S3-MINI'. Flag if 'C6' or 'WROOM' found on this board.

title: Digital sensor modules (24-pin, EPS, PCIe): ESP32-C6-MINI-1 (v3.10)
rule: The 24-pin ATX, EPS 8-pin, and PCIe 8-pin modules must use ESP32-C6-MINI-1-N4 (LCSC C5736265), per v3.10 specification. ESP32-S3-MINI-1 is the as-built part on the 24-pin ATX only (still pending migration per action item -1).
scope: Boards: eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port: assert MCU Value='ESP32-C6-MINI-1*'. Board: atx-24pin: currently S3-MINI-1 (migration pending — flag as advisory not hard until migrated).
rationale: v3.10 consolidation: EPS/PCIe/24-pin move to ESP32-C6-MINI-1 (C3-MINI-compatible footprint; lower cost). C6 has sufficient GPIOs for I2C INA238 + §6.13 front-end + CAN + USB.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.10 note — 'the three digital-sensor Standard modules (24-pin, EPS, PCIe) move ESP32-S3-MINI-1 -> ESP32-C6-MINI-1'
check_method: For boards eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-*: assert U1 Value contains 'C6-MINI-1', LCSC=C5736265. For atx-24pin: flag if still S3-MINI-1 (advisory until migrated).

title: EPS/PCIe §6.13 detection front-end: INA181A2 + TLV7011 per cable
rule: EPS 8-pin and PCIe 8-pin modules must include per-cable: one INA181A2IDBVR (gain-50 CSA, LCSC C2058784) and one TLV7011DBVR (hysteresis comparator, LCSC C702117). These form the transient DETECTION front-end (INA181 -> TLV7011 -> firmware THRESH -> FREEZE trigger).
scope: Boards: eps-8pin, pcie-8pin-2port, pcie-8pin-3port. Count INA181* = number of cables. Count TLV7011* = number of cables. Assert equal to cable count.
rationale: v3.10 §6.13 transient-visibility ladder: the detection front-end flags transients as BINARY events and ORs into the FREEZE trigger. Without it EPS/PCIe cannot flag transients at all.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.10 note — '§6.13 EPS/PCIe transient-visibility ladder... INA181-class CSA + hysteresis comparator -> firmware-settable threshold -> ORs into the §6.10 FREEZE trigger'
check_method: Count INA181* and TLV7011* in nl.comps for EPS/PCIe boards. Assert each equals cable count (2 for 2-port, 3 for 3-port/EPS).

title: 12VHPWR: 4 sideband pins (S1-S4) pass through J3→J4 AND tap ESP32 GPIOs
rule: The 12V-2x6 connector sideband pins (SENSE0/S1, SENSE1/S2, CARD_PWR_STABLE/S3, CARD_CBL_PRES#/S4, connector pins 13-16) must: (a) pass through from J3 to J4 (the cable interposer function), AND (b) each tap a free ESP32-S3 GPIO via a 1kΩ series resistor (R10-R13) for firmware readout.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. Sideband nets (SENSE0, SENSE1, CARD_PWR_STABLE, CARD_CBL_PRES#) must connect J3 pin 13-16, J4 pin 13-16, and ESP32 GPIO nets via 1kΩ resistors.
rationale: v3.4: sideband taps let firmware read cable's advertised power capability + present/stable state and report over CAN. Passthrough preserves the host GPU sideband signaling.
source: CLAUDE.md module sensing — 'The four 12V-2x6 sideband sense pins (13-16: SENSE0, SENSE1, CARD_PWR_STABLE, CARD_CBL_PRES#) now pass through J3->J4 AND each taps a free ESP32-S3 GPIO (IO8/9/11/12) via a 1k series R (R10-R13)'
check_method: Board=12vhpwr-standard: for each sideband net, verify it appears on J3, J4, and a 1kΩ resistor leading to an ESP GPIO net.

title: 24-pin ATX module: J3 and J4 are Molex 5569 24-circuit MALE right-angle headers
rule: The 24-pin ATX module PSU-side power path must use two Molex 5569 24-circuit MALE right-angle headers (J3=PSU-side input, J4=motherboard-side output). Both headers are male — no female receptacle exists as a standard board-mount part. A bridging female-to-female cable connects J4 to the motherboard.
scope: Board: atx-24pin. J3 and J4 footprints must contain '5569' or 'Mini-Fit' and be 24-circuit male.
rationale: §2.8 LOCKED: 'TWO Molex Mini-Fit Jr (5569) 24-circuit MALE headers: input J3 (PSU side) and output J4 (motherboard side)... both module connectors are male'
source: CLAUDE.md §2.8 connector section — '24-pin ATX module is a power-path interposer with TWO Molex Mini-Fit Jr (5569) 24-circuit MALE headers'
check_method: Board=atx-24pin: J3 and J4 footprints must contain '5569' or 'Mini-Fit'. Assert count=2 such connectors (24-pin, right-angle, male).

title: 12VHPWR connector: Molex 2191161161; pins 1-6=+12V, 7-12=GND, 13-16=sideband
rule: The 12V-2x6 connector on 12VHPWR modules must be Molex 219116 / 2191161161 (PCIe CEM5 right-angle THT). Pin assignment: 1-6=+12V (row adjacent to signal pins), 7-12=GND (outer row), 13-16=sideband S1-S4. This polarity is critical — swapping it shorts +12V to GND.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard, 12vhpwr-pro. Connector footprint=CEC_12V2x6_Horizontal. Net on pins 1-6 must be +12V; pins 7-12 must be GND.
rationale: §2.8 SAFETY note: the connector is symmetric — +12V vs GND is a system/CEM assignment. The schematic ties 7-12 to GND plane; verify before powering.
source: CLAUDE.md §2.8 — 'pins 1-6 = +12V (the row ADJACENT to the signal pins), 7-12 = GND (the OUTER row), 13-16 = sideband S1..S4. SAFETY: the connector is symmetric... VERIFY pins 7-12 = GND'
check_method: For J3/J4 with footprint CEC_12V2x6: net_of(J,'1'-'6') must contain '+12V' or '12V'; net_of(J,'7'-'12') must be GND.

title: EPS/PCIe power connectors: GND on pins 1-4, +12V on pins 5-8
rule: EPS 8-pin module connectors J_IN/J_OUT must use Molex 87427-0802 (no snap pegs). PCIe 8-pin connectors must use Molex 45586-0005. Pin polarity: pins 1-4=GND, pins 5-8=+12V (SENSEC*_HI). This is the CORRECTED assignment — the original generator had it backwards (+12V on 1-4).
scope: Boards: eps-8pin (Molex 87427), pcie-8pin-* (Molex 45586). For each J_IN/J_OUT: net_of(J,'1'-'4') must be GND; net_of(J,'5'-'8') must contain +12V/SENSEC.
rationale: EPS12V/EATX12V standard: GND on pins 1-4, +12V on 5-8. Reversed polarity causes catastrophic PSU/motherboard short on power-up.
source: CLAUDE.md EPS pinout fix — 'Corrected to GND on pads 1-4, +12V on pads 5-8 in the schematic... gen-modules.py (PINMAP)'
check_method: For J_IN*/J_OUT* connectors on EPS/PCIe boards: net_of(J,'1') through net_of(J,'4') in GND nets. net_of(J,'5') through net_of(J,'8') in SENSEC*_HI or +12V nets.

title: Schematic ERC must be clean (zero real violations)
rule: ERC must report zero violations after filtering benign types: lib_symbol_mismatch (generator cache drift), unconnected_wire_endpoint (documented Hub off-grid flag stamps). All other ERC violations are real and must be resolved.
scope: All boards. Run kicad-cli sch erc --format json and filter BENIGN_ERC types.
rationale: ERC violations indicate real connectivity errors (unconnected pins, power-rail type mismatches) that would cause board failures.
source: CLAUDE.md commands — 'kicad-cli sch erc --exit-code-violations --format json -o erc.json'
check_method: Run ERC JSON. Filter out lib_symbol_mismatch and unconnected_wire_endpoint. Assert remaining violations == 0.

title: No single-node nets (unconnected pins forming dead-end signals)
rule: Every net that is not an intentional no-connect must have at least 2 nodes. Single-node nets indicate a missing connection (e.g., a schematic pin with a dangling wire that never reaches its partner).
scope: All boards: any net in the netlist with exactly 1 node, excluding nets whose name starts with 'unconnected-' or 'Net-' (KiCad NC markers).
rationale: A single-node net is a real schematic connectivity defect — the pin has no driver or load. This will cause functional failure on the assembled board.
source: CLAUDE.md verification checklist — implied by ERC clean requirement; chk_no_unconnected in cec_synth_pipeline.py
check_method: For all nets in nl.nets: if len(nodes)==1 and net not starting with 'unconnected-'/'Net-', flag as violation.

title: All library paths must use ${KIPRJMOD}-relative paths with cec-* nicknames
rule: Every sym-lib-table and fp-lib-table entry must use ${KIPRJMOD} as the path root (no absolute paths, no ${KICAD*_3DMODEL_DIR}). Library nicknames must be prefixed 'cec' or 'cec-*' (e.g., cec-Package_SO, cec-Resistor_SMD). A bare stock nickname collides with machine-global KiCad libraries.
scope: All boards: sym-lib-table, fp-lib-table files. Check (uri ...) entries for absolute paths or ${KICAD*} env vars. Check (name ...) entries for bare stock nicknames.
rationale: A machine-global library with the same bare name shadows the in-repo copy on other machines, causing footprint/symbol lookup failures (this bit the project once with Package_SO and INA228 footprints).
source: CLAUDE.md KiCad environment — 'Library-table NICKNAMES must be namespaced cec / cec-*... Never reference ${KICAD*_3DMODEL_DIR} or absolute paths'
check_method: Parse sym-lib-table / fp-lib-table. For each entry: assert uri contains '${KIPRJMOD}'. Assert name starts with 'cec'. Flag any absolute path or bare stock nickname.

title: Hub Standard: SK6812 LED data line must go through SN74AHCT1G08 level shifter
rule: The Hub Standard must include U6 = SN74AHCT1G08 (single 2-input AND gate used as buffer, SOT-23-5, VCC=+5VSB) between the ESP32 GPIO and DL1.DIN (LED data). A 330Ω series resistor (R14) must follow before DL1.DIN. No direct GPIO→LED connection is acceptable.
scope: Board: hub-standard. Verify SN74AHCT1G08 (or 1G08) present on LED_DATA net path. Verify 330Ω R14 on DIN net.
rationale: ESP32's 3.3V GPIO output is below SK6812 V_IH minimum (0.7×VDD=3.5V at 5V). Without the level shifter, LED data may not register reliably causing flickering or no-op commands.
source: CLAUDE.md Hub Standard — 'SK6812 data level shift (2026-06-05): the ESP32's 3.3V GPIO is below the 5V SK6812 V_IH (0.7*VDD ~= 3.5V)... U6 (SN74AHCT1G08)'
check_method: Board=hub-standard: assert any Value containing '74AHCT1G08' or '1G08' on LED_DATA net. Assert 330Ω R on the DIN side.

title: Hub Standard: LP5907 LDO for 3.3V generation
rule: Hub Standard must use LP5907MFX as its 3.3V LDO regulator (LCSC C80670). The LP5907 has no BYP pin (pin 4 is NC — do not connect it).
scope: Board: hub-standard. BOM must include LP5907. LCSC=C80670.
rationale: v1.1 decisions carry forward. LP5907 is a low-noise LDO suitable for the ADC supply domain.
source: CLAUDE.md Hub Standard — 'LP5907 LDO'; Hub Standard BOM section — 'LP5907 C80670'
check_method: Board=hub-standard: assert any Value='LP5907*'. LCSC=C80670.

title: Hub Standard: 4700µF hold-up capacitor must be aluminum electrolytic (not polymer)
rule: Hub Standard C1 hold-up capacitor must be 4700µF aluminum electrolytic, specifically Panasonic EEVFK1C472M (16V). It must NOT be a polymer capacitor. The spec previously said 'polymer' — that was corrected in v1.9.
scope: Board: hub-standard. C1: assert Value='4700uF' or similar, and BOM description/footprint indicates aluminum electrolytic, LCSC part is EEVFK1C472M.
rationale: The hold-up capacitor must survive voltage transients during hot-plug and supply the FLASH write hold-up (OQ-56). Aluminum electrolytic has the right ESR/ESL and temperature rating; polymer was specified in error.
source: CLAUDE.md Hub Standard — '4700 uF aluminum electrolytic hold-up — Panasonic EEVFK1C472M 16V, corrected from polymer v1.9'
check_method: Board=hub-standard: C1 Value contains '4700'. BOM MPN/manufacturer contains 'EEVFK1C472M' or 'Panasonic'. Flag if described as 'polymer'.

title: Hub Standard NanoKVM aux connector: S5B-PH-K-S right-angle 5-pin JST-PH
rule: Hub Standard J7 NanoKVM aux connector must be the right-angle S5B-PH-K-S (LCSC C157923, footprint JST_PH_S5B-PH-K-S_1x05_P2.00mm_Horizontal). NOT the top-entry B5B-PH-K-S (C157993) — that is the vertical version rejected in v3.9.
scope: Board: hub-standard. J7 BOM: LCSC=C157923, footprint must contain 'S5B' or 'Horizontal'. Assert NOT 'B5B' or 'vertical'.
rationale: v3.9 LOCKED: right-angle form so the NanoKVM cable exits a board edge and runs parallel to the board (vertical B5B needed headroom a cased Hub does not have).
source: CLAUDE.md v3.9 — 'J7 (NanoKVM aux) is the RIGHT-ANGLE S5B-PH-K-S (LCSC C157923)... NOT the top-entry B5B-PH-K-S'
check_method: Board=hub-standard, J7: LCSC=C157923. Footprint contains 'S5B-PH-K-S' or 'Horizontal'. Flag if 'B5B-PH-K-S' or 'C157993'.

title: Hub NanoKVM UART has 33Ω series resistors; KVM_3V3_REF uses ratiometric ADC dividers
rule: Hub Standard NanoKVM UART TX/RX must go through 33Ω series resistors (R19, R20) to ESP32 IO11/IO12. The KVM_3V3_REF pin (J7 pin 5) must be sensed ratiometrically: 47k/10k divider (R21/R22) → ADC1 IO1, AND Hub's own 3.3V through 47k/10k (R23/R24) → ADC1 IO2. ESD diode D7 (PESD5V0S1BA) must clamp the cabled KVM_3V3_REF pin.
scope: Board: hub-standard. R19/R20 on UART nets. R21-R24 dividers on KVM_3V3_REF and +3V3 nets. D7 PESD5V0S1BA on KVM_3V3_REF.
rationale: 33Ω UART protection prevents ESD/latch-up on the UART pins from the NanoKVM cable. Ratiometric sensing of the KVM 3V3 reference detects a sagging rail without trusting it as a reference (per user: 'can't trust the 3v3 beyond a shadow of a doubt').
source: CLAUDE.md action item 0(a) — 'R19/R20 -> ESP IO11/IO12... R21/R22 -> ADC1 IO1, AND the Hub's OWN +3V3 via an identical 47k/10k (R23/R24) -> ADC1 IO2'
check_method: Board=hub-standard: assert R19/R20 ~33Ω on UART TX/RX nets. Assert R21/R22 ~47k/10k on KVM_3V3_REF net. Assert R23/R24 ~47k/10k on +3V3 net. Assert D7=PESD5V0S1BA on KVM_3V3_REF.

title: Hub Standard: USBLC6-2SC6 ESD protection on USB D+/D- lines
rule: Hub Standard must include USBLC6-2SC6 (or equivalent dual-line USB ESD device) on the USB_D_P and USB_D_N lines.
scope: Board: hub-standard. Find any USBLC6* in BOM. Assert it is on USB_D_P/USB_D_N nets.
rationale: USB connector is user-facing — ESD events from hot-plugging are common. The USBLC6-2SC6 provides <1pF/line protection suitable for USB Full-Speed.
source: CLAUDE.md Hub Standard BOM sourcing — 'USBLC6-2SC6'; vendor audit confirms correct pinout for D+/D-
check_method: Board=hub-standard: assert any Value='USBLC6*'. Verify on USB_D_P / USB_D_N nets.

title: M3 mounting holes must be chassis-grounded (GND-connected copper pads)
rule: All M3 mounting holes on all boards must use the MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via footprint (copper pad + via, not the plain NPTH variant) and must be connected to GND in the netlist.
scope: All boards. All H* / MK* references with mounting hole footprints: assert net = GND. Assert footprint contains 'Pad_Via' or equivalent.
rationale: §4 (Hub Standard): '4x M3 chassis-grounded mounting'. GND-connected mounting holes provide chassis bonding for EMC and ESD return path.
source: CLAUDE.md Hub Standard — '4x M3 chassis-grounded mounting'; PCB layout toolkit note on MountingHole_3.2mm_M3_Pad_Via
check_method: For all H*/MK* refs in nl.comps: assert footprint contains 'Pad' (not plain NPTH). Assert at least one pad on GND net.

title: BOOT/RESET buttons must be TS-1088-AR02016 (not Panasonic EVQ)
rule: BOOT (SW1) and RESET (SW2) buttons on all boards must be TS-1088-AR02016 (XKB, LCSC C720477). The Panasonic EVQ (EVQPUJ/EVQPUA) is explicitly replaced — it uses a different 4-pad footprint vs the TS-1088's 2-pad, so it is not a drop-in and cannot be silently substituted.
scope: All boards: SW1, SW2. BOM LCSC=C720477. Footprint must be 2-pad TS-1088 land.
rationale: Hub Standard BOM sourcing: SW1/2 changed from EVQ to TS-1088-AR02016. EPS and 12VHPWR also updated. The EVQ's 4-pad land is incompatible with the 2-pad TS-1088 footprint.
source: CLAUDE.md Hub Standard BOM sourcing — 'SW1/2 EVQ->TS-1088-AR02016 (C720477)'; EPS update — 'BOOT/RESET buttons SW1/SW2 Panasonic_EVQPUJ_EVQPUA -> TS-1088-AR02016 (C720477)'
check_method: For SW1/SW2: assert LCSC=C720477 or Value contains 'TS-1088'. Flag any Value containing 'EVQ'.

title: All modules must have USB-C flash/debug front-end (J5, SW1/SW2, D2, CC resistors)
rule: Every generated module must include: USB-C connector J5 (ESP native USB D+/D-), BOOT button SW1 (GPIO0), RESET button SW2 (EN), SS34 ORing Schottky D2, 10µF bulk capacitor C9 on VBUS, CC1/CC2 5.1kΩ pull-down resistors R8/R9.
scope: All module boards (not Hub). Verify J5=USB-C, SW1/SW2 present, D2=SS34 or similar, C9>=10µF on VBUS, R8/R9=5.1kΩ on CC1/CC2.
rationale: Every module must be independently flashable in the field. The USB-C front-end provides a complete flash path without any external adapter.
source: CLAUDE.md 'Flash/debug front end added to ALL generated modules (2026-06-04, gen-modules BASE_PARTS)'
check_method: For each module board: assert J5 footprint contains 'USB' or 'TYPE_C'. Assert SW1/SW2 present. Assert D2 on VBUS net with Schottky part. Assert R8/R9 ~5.1kΩ on CC1/CC2 nets.

title: 12VHPWR Standard rail divider R5/R6: must be 0.1% tolerance resistors
rule: The 47kΩ (R5, Yageo RT0402BRD0747KL, LCSC C728561) and 10kΩ (R6, Yageo RT0402BRD0710KL, LCSC C190095) rail voltage divider resistors on the 12VHPWR Standard module must be 0.1% tolerance (25ppm). 1% resistors are NOT acceptable for this divider — the REF3030 ratiometric reference does not cancel divider-ratio error.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. R5 (47kΩ): assert LCSC=C728561 or Tolerance=0.1%. R6 (10kΩ): assert LCSC=C190095 or Tolerance=0.1%.
rationale: v3.8: 'the REF3030 ratiometric ref does NOT cancel divider-ratio error, so 0.1% is required for the ~0.3-0.5% V channel'. 1% divider error dominates the measurement budget.
source: CLAUDE.md 12VHPWR Standard BOM — 'Repointed R5 -> Yageo RT0402BRD0747KL (C728561, 47k 0.1% 25ppm) and R6 -> RT0402BRD0710KL (C190095, 10k 0.1% 25ppm)'
check_method: Board=12vhpwr-standard: R5 LCSC=C728561 and R6 LCSC=C190095, OR BOM Tolerance field contains '0.1%'. Flag if 1% Tolerance.

title: 12VHPWR Standard: 10Ω RFH/RFL + 470nF CF input RC filters on each INA240 channel
rule: Each of the 6 INA240 channels on the 12VHPWR Standard module must have: 10Ω series resistors on both IN+ and IN- inputs (RFH/RFL, 0.1% tolerance, Yageo RT0402BRE0710RL, LCSC C705642) and a 470nF differential capacitor (CF) across the filtered inputs. This creates fc≈16.9kHz matching the §6.10 acquisition bandwidth.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. Count RFH*/RFL* = 12 (2 per channel × 6 channels). Count CF* = 6. Assert values 10Ω and 470nF respectively.
rationale: v3.4: input RC filter prevents HF aliasing into the ESP32 SAR ADC. 10Ω limit matches TI INA240 input resistance ceiling for negligible gain/CMRR error. The 0.1% tolerance maintains AC CMRR on the transient capture.
source: CLAUDE.md module sensing — 'per-channel INA240 input anti-alias/transient RC filter — matched 10 ohm series Rf on each input (RFH/RFL1-6) + a 470nF differential cap (CF1-6)'
check_method: Board=12vhpwr-standard: count RFH*/RFL* with value ~10Ω, assert=12. Count CF* ~470nF, assert=6. LCSC C705642 for the 10Ω 0.1% parts.

title: 12VHPWR Standard: 2× NTC thermistors (TH1 board/shunt temp, TH2 ambient)
rule: 12VHPWR Standard module must include two NTC thermistors: TH1 (Murata NCP15XH103F03RC, LCSC C77131, footprint NTC_0402_1005Metric) at the shunt row measuring board/shunt temperature, and TH2 measuring ambient. Each uses a 10kΩ high-side divider and 100nF filter cap into ADC2 IO13/IO14 respectively.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. Assert TH1 and TH2 (Thermistor_NTC or NCP15XH103F03RC) present. LCSC=C77131 for both.
rationale: v3.7: 'the 12VHPWR Standard module gains two NTC thermistor dividers... reporting temperature + dT-above-ambient'. Compensates INA240 gain drift and shunt TCR. The INA240 has no die-temp sensor.
source: CLAUDE.md v3.7 — 'TH1 by the shunt row = board/shunt temp, TH2 ambient... into spare ESP32-S3 ADC2 IO13/IO14'
check_method: Board=12vhpwr-standard: assert TH1 and TH2 present (Value='NCP15XH103F03RC' or 'Thermistor_NTC'). LCSC=C77131. Assert on IO13 and IO14 nets respectively.

title: 12VHPWR Standard: 1nF C0G cap on VRAIL_DIV node
rule: The VRAIL_DIV node (junction of R5/R6 divider feeding ADC IO7) must have a 1nF C0G (NP0) bypass capacitor (C24, Murata GRM1555C1H102JA01D, LCSC C76947) to GND. This provides fc≈19kHz S&H charge and matches the INA240 channel bandwidth.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. VRAIL_DIV net must have a ~1nF C0G cap to GND.
rationale: The ESP32 SAR ADC S&H capacitor needs charge from the source. Without the ADC input cap the S&H settling time at 47k||10k source impedance is too slow for accurate readings.
source: CLAUDE.md 12VHPWR BOM — 'added C24 = 1nF C0G (Murata GRM1555C1H102JA01D / C76947) VRAIL_DIV->GND, fc~19kHz'
check_method: Board=12vhpwr-standard: on VRAIL_DIV net, find cap ~1nF. Assert LCSC=C76947 or Value='1nF' with C0G/NP0 dielectric.

title: Hub Standard BOM cost target: ~$36 at 100 quantity
rule: The Hub Standard BOM total (parts only, JLCPCB single-qty as proxy) should be approximately $36 at 100-quantity production. Significant drift (>20%) from this target is a design flag.
scope: Board: hub-standard. BOM CSV total cost field. ~$12/board parts at single-qty JLCPCB (as-sourced).
rationale: §9 BOM targets define the competitive positioning of each tier. Exceeding the target without a spec revision signals a component selection error or scope creep.
source: CLAUDE.md boards table — 'Hub Standard: BOM target (100q) ~$36'; BOM sourcing note — '~$12.11/board parts'
check_method: Sum BOM JLCPCB unit prices × qty for all sourced parts. Flag if >$43 (120% of target) or <$25 (implausibly low).

title: 24-pin ATX module BOM cost target: ~$35+ at 100 quantity
rule: The 24-pin ATX module BOM should be approximately $35+ (above the pre-INA228 baseline of $35, with modest increase expected from 4× INA228 over INA238). Flag significant overrun.
scope: Board: atx-24pin. BOM total vs $35 baseline.
rationale: §9 BOM target. The INA228 adds some cost over INA238 per the spec note '*The 24-pin $35 target predates the v1.4 move to four INA228 parts'.
source: CLAUDE.md boards table — '24-pin ATX module: BOM target (100q) $35*'
check_method: Sum BOM unit prices. Flag if >$50 (significant overrun from INA228 cost delta).

title: EPS 8-pin module BOM cost target: ~$32 at 100 quantity
rule: The EPS 8-pin module BOM should be approximately $32 at 100-quantity production.
scope: Board: eps-8pin. BOM total vs $32 target.
rationale: §9 BOM target for standard-tier cable module.
source: CLAUDE.md boards table — 'EPS 8-pin module: BOM target (100q) $32'
check_method: Sum BOM unit prices. Flag if >$39 (>20% over target).

title: 12VHPWR Standard module BOM cost target: ~$49 at 100 quantity
rule: The 12VHPWR Standard module BOM should be approximately $49 at 100-quantity production. The as-sourced single-qty JLCPCB parts total is ~$21.
scope: Board: 12vhpwr-standard. BOM total vs $49 target.
rationale: §9 BOM target. Cost is dominated by 6× INA240A3DR (~$1.87 each), ESP32, and 6× 1mΩ shunts.
source: CLAUDE.md boards table — '12VHPWR Standard module: BOM target (100q) $49'; BOM sourcing — '~$21/board JLC parts (single-qty)'
check_method: Sum BOM unit prices. Flag if >$59 (>20% over target).

title: No distributed voltage reference on Standard-tier: pin 7 stays reserved spare
rule: Standard-tier modules must NOT include a distributed voltage reference on pin 7 of the RJ-45 interface. OQ-3 resolved: local REF3033 on each Pro module; no distributed reference; pin 7 is a reserved spare. A local reference (like REF3030 on 12VHPWR-Std) is acceptable — the prohibition is on using pin 7 as a distributed reference bus.
scope: All module boards: pin 7 net must NOT be 'AUX_REF' or 'VREF' or any reference bus name. Already covered by rj45-pin7-reserved-not-aux-ref but stated separately for clarity.
rationale: OQ-3 RESOLVED v1.1: a distributed reference would couple noise across modules, create ground-loop sensitivity to cable length, and require matched cable impedance across the platform.
source: CLAUDE.md OQ-3 — 'RESOLVED, v1.1: Precision reference path. Local REF3033 on each Pro module; NO distributed reference; pin 7 is a reserved spare. Do not treat pin 7 as AUX_REF anymore.'
check_method: Same as rj45-pin7-reserved-not-aux-ref: net_of(J1,'7') must not match AUX|REF. Additionally check no cross-module reference bus nets exist.
existing_checker: chk_pin_allocation in cec_synth_pipeline.py CONFORMANCE stage (covers pin 7 AUX|REF check)

title: Hub Standard must have 4 DETECT ESD diodes (D2-D5, one per port)
rule: Hub Standard must carry exactly 4 ESD diodes on its 4 DETECT lines (one per RJ-45 port J2-J5): D2, D3, D4, D5 = PESD5V0S1BA (SOD-323, LCSC C5261083). Each diode cathode connects to the port's DETECT line; anode to GND.
scope: Board: hub-standard. Count PESD5V0S1BA diodes. Assert count=4. Assert each on a distinct DETECT net.
rationale: Hub Standard has 4 ports; each port's DETECT pin connects directly to an ESP32 ADC. All 4 lines need ESD protection for hot-plug insertion.
source: CLAUDE.md locked decisions — 'Hub Standard now populates this pin-8 ESD diode — D2-D5, PESD5V0S1BA in SOD-323, one per port'
check_method: Board=hub-standard: count refs D2/D3/D4/D5. Assert Value=PESD5V0S1BA, LCSC=C5261083. Assert each on a different DETECT* net.
